clue.text: Swollen account was due payment

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
money that was due was owed

explanation.surface: Someone's bill has swollen because a payment was overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails that have filled out with wind have puffed up, the same as swollen.

clue.text: Printer powered by a liquid engine

parts.note: ink is a liquid used for writing and printing
a jet is a type of aircraft engine

explanation.surface: A printing machine that runs on some fluid-driven motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A common type of computer printer squirts tiny droplets onto paper.

clue.text: Feeling unwell in the French town

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
feeling unwell means ill

explanation.surface: Someone feels poorly while staying in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'town' is generous: Lille is a large city in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large urban place in northern France, so a town in the loose sense.

clue.text: Weak English bishop danced like a duck!

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to foot it is to dance, so footed means danced

explanation.surface: A feeble English clergyman waddled about like a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks have skin joining their toes, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Violent doctor Crippen starts drinking wine

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the wine goes inside the other letters
the start of the word Crippen is its first letter

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: The notorious murderer Dr Crippen turns violent once he takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts the wine inside DR + C. Hawley Crippen was a notorious Edwardian murderer in London, which makes 'doctor' read as his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and forceful, close to violent.

clue.text: Arrange to rob Leo during the dance

indicators.note: arrange tells us the letters of rob Leo are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to mug a man called Leo while he is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish dance in triple time, made famous by Ravel's piece.

clue.text: Prohibit company banking money

parts.note: to ban something is to prohibit it

explanation.surface: Stopping a firm from doing business in banking.
explanation.definitionFit: Banco is the term for bank money, a bank's notional currency as distinct from cash, and a gambler's call to stake the whole bank.

clue.text: Special poets are honoured people

explanation.surface: Poets of distinction are the ones who receive honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets appointed to a royal post are laureates, and the word also means anyone given an award or prize, such as Nobel winners.

clue.text: Diamond, timber, asbestos

parts.note: rock is slang for a diamond
timber is wood

explanation.surface: A list of building materials: gem, lumber and a fireproof mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockwood is an old name for a woody-looking fibrous variety of the mineral.

clue.text: Weather research centre that's out of this world

parts.note: the sky is where weather happens
a lab, short for laboratory, is a research centre

explanation.surface: Praise for a meteorological institute that is simply superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' looks like praise, but literally means in orbit: the American space station of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a US orbiting laboratory, quite literally beyond our planet.

clue.text: Declare her weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name, so it can stand for 'her'
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A request that a woman state how heavy she is.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to make it known publicly, to proclaim it.

clue.text: Move the box to the left by thought alone

parts.note: the box is slang for television, the tele
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Telekinesis: shifting the TV set leftwards with mental power alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by thought alone' finishes the definition, since teleporting is moving something by the power of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To teleport is to transport instantly, in science fiction often by mental power.

clue.text: Blow using fists' digits

parts.note: a digit is a single number, and one is a number
two is also a single number

explanation.surface: A punch made with the fingers of the hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digits' looks like fingers but means numbers here, giving two numbers in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing it is a quick pair of punches, left jab then right cross.

clue.text: Premonition that no one retreats after worker, here in France, joins Patrick

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect
ici is French for 'here'
Pat is short for Patrick

indicators.note: retreats means goes backwards, so the words no one are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tangled story of a foreboding involving a labourer in France and a man called Patrick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns NO + I into ION, which goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipation is a sense of what is coming, a foreboding of the future.

clue.text: Take windy Rome road east to the airfield

indicators.note: windy means twisting and winding, so the letters of Rome road are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Directions: follow the winding Rome road east to reach the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is a small airport, a place where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: To become a scientist, doctor gets a name change to the street

indicators.note: change to tells us one part of a word is swapped for something new

parts.note: a physician is a medical doctor
A plus N, the abbreviation for name
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A doctor changes their name by deed poll and moves street to become a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change to' replaces the AN at the end of PHYSICIAN with ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A physicist studies matter and energy, a branch of science.

clue.text: Crazy pets made a sudden rush

indicators.note: crazy suggests things going haywire, so the letters of pets made are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mad animals launched a sudden charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a headlong panicked charge, usually by a herd of animals.

clue.text: Lady Prescott transported some flying reptiles!

indicators.note: transported suggests carried somewhere else, so the letters of Lady Prescott are moved around

explanation.surface: The wife of a politician carried off by prehistoric winged creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Prescott suggests the wife of John Prescott, a former British Deputy Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterodactyls were winged creatures of the dinosaur age.

clue.text: Can a staff cook stomach game?

indicators.note: to stomach is to hold within, so the answer is held in the words Can a staff cook

explanation.surface: A question whether a chef can stomach cooking wild game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like meat for a cook, but it is a card game; the answer begins the words 'Can a staff'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: The present Maureen intended, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: Mo is short for Maureen, and intended means meant

explanation.surface: A gift that a woman called Maureen meant to give, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The present' looks like a gift, but means the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment is the here and now, the current instant in time.

clue.text: In the middle of the morning I would have a piece of crust

parts.note: AM stands for the morning hours
I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: a piece of means a small part taken from inside the word crust

explanation.surface: Someone having a bit of bread crust around mid-morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means among or surrounded by, the same as being in the middle of.

clue.text: Annoyed when obliged to accept a rule

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: if you are tied to something you are obliged to do it

explanation.surface: Someone irritated at being forced to go along with a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To try someone's patience is to irritate them, so a tried person is vexed.

clue.text: Corner location houses first class new section on cotton fabric

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: a nook is a corner or recess
A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb about a corner plot with a new wing above a cotton mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' wraps the corner around the other pieces, splitting it after its first letter. A1 is British slang for top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Nainsook is a fine soft muslin from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Nod so violently and it might fall off a girl's head

definitions.text: it might fall off a girl's head

indicators.note: violently suggests shaking hard, so the letters of nod so are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Nod your head too hard and your hair net could slip off.
explanation.definitionFit: A snood is a hair net or bag worn at the back of a woman's head.

clue.text: Sort of exercises that make Boris ache badly after an hour's gone

indicators.note: badly suggests disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
gone means removed, so a letter is taken away

explanation.surface: Workouts leave Boris aching terribly once an hour is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes H from BORISACHE, leaving BORISACE; 'badly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobics is a type of vigorous rhythmic workout to boost heart and lungs.

clue.text: An evening worker

parts.note: looks like someone on the night shift, but evening means making things even, smoothing creases from clothes

explanation.surface: Someone who works the late shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the time of day but the act of making something flat and even.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presses laundry smooths out the creases.

clue.text: Very famous member's death

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
death is one's end

explanation.surface: The passing of a celebrated club member.
explanation.definitionFit: In casual use, someone famous enough to be talked of in stories is a legend, as in 'a legend in their own lifetime'.

clue.text: Tied to an awful counteracting agent

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the letters of tied to an are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bound to a dreadful opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that neutralises a poison.
